comment: Control keys on Linux (docs/linux/IMPLEMENTATION.md B.2). Every gammaos-nano.rc trigger, every rc trigger
elsewhere in the patch that names one of Nano's keys, every framework listener of Nano's keys and init's own
control keys get a row; tools/nano-tree/nanotree/controlkeys.py derives them and
tools/nano-tree/tests/test_control_keys.py fails on a missing or stale row.
match: a trigger (its conditions joined by ' && ', property:K=V written K=V) or a key; 'prefix.*' covers keys.
disposition: routed (route: session:<verb> a thimsy-session request, session-key the session reads the key
itself, launcher, hook:<action> the family hook, first-frame, rc-reset only the rc's reset), store-only (state:
the store keeps it, nothing else happens), refused (an Android-only message: logged once), not-reached (no
writer on Linux). value: for a key row, the value that triggers (default any). reset: written back first, as
the rc does. source manual: a listener the patch does not show (GammaOS base code), with the reason in note.
Routed and refused single-key rows are also rows of kControlRows in nano/platform/linux/ControlKeys.cpp.

rows.note: apexd is Android's; the rc re-sends input uevents after its flood. Linux: mdev and thimsy-padd own the input nodes.

The kernel wakes the device (power key, lid) and thimsy-session restores it; only the rc's reset is mirrored.
